doc.title: Rossano Sportiello interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, October 2, 2015 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Rock, heavy metal and wanting to make people dream
summary: He did not relate to aggressive music and violent media and says his aim is to make people dream and feel lighter.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Was there, when you were playing these gigs as a teenager, what was considered rock & roll?

Well this opens another — because for example when I was a teenager in Italy there was also this big wave of the so-called heavy metal music. So when we said rock & roll we even considered that being part of it. And I have to say that I could never relate to that kind of music that pounds way too much, said in very plain words. Very aggressive music in general. I don’t relate to that at all. I think for the way I am and, once more, I want to make sure that that’s just my opinion, I don’t want to impose any of my ideas, but I think that I have to try to make the people dream, as a musician. I want to try to give the people some nice feelings. Because we are surrounded by garbage and nasty things all around constantly. As soon as you turn on the TV you have that pounding stuff. Very bad things happening in the world. You know you cannot watch anymore, a movie, without seeing someone getting killed. This is the most absurd nonsense. I don’t get it. The

governments, they make so many laws and this, they should prevent whoever, 99% of the stuff on TV about violence and killing. You know, because then once after, I’m going to get up and shoot the people. That’s where they get the inspiration I guess. So I think that as a musician in my small, in a very humble way, I want to make people dream. I want to make people feel lighter. That’s what I want to do. So it might be wrong or right I don’t care. That’s what I want to do.
Well said. You made me feel lighter yesterday when I was listening to “St. Louis Blues.”
